question: The chemical formula of glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆. The weight % of carbon in glucose is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**40%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
• The molar mass of glucose can be calculated by summing the molar masses of its constituent elements: Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), and Oxygen (O).
 
• To find the percentage of carbon in glucose, the mass of carbon atoms in one mole of glucose is divided by the molar mass of glucose and then multiplied by 100.
 
• This gives the weight percentage of carbon in glucose as 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Formula**

 
 
• The molecular formula of a compound gives the exact number of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound.
 
• For glucose, the molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass**
 
 
• The molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance (chemical element or chemical compound).
 
• The molar masses of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are approximately 12 g/mol, 1 g/mol, and 16 g/mol, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Percentage Composition by Mass**
 
 
• The percentage composition by mass of an element in a compound is the percentage by mass of that element in the compound.
 
• It is calculated as (mass of the element in 1 mole of the compound / molar mass of the compound) × 100.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Weight % of Carbon in Glucose**
 
 
• The molar mass of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) = (6 × 12) + (12 × 1) + (6 × 16) = 180 g/mol.
 
• The mass of carbon in one mole of glucose = 6 × 12 = 72 g.
 
• Weight % of carbon in glucose = (72 g / 180 g) × 100 = 40%.
